svg.aria-label: QBM-08 · From magnetic environment to plant phenotype
svg.text: QBM-08 · From magnetic environment to plant phenotype
The review's integrated model — an architecture for designing experiments, not a demonstrated causal network

g.title: Near-null magnetic field (< 1 uT) tier T4 (verified) quantum class: structural_context
Geomagnetic field (25-65 uT) tier T4 (verified) quantum class: structural_context

Cryptochrome 1 (CRY1) tier T1 (verified) quantum class: radical_pair_acceptor, flavin_semiquinone, triplet_yield_sensitive nuclei: 1H, 14N AGI: AT4G08920 Ahmad2007: Magnetic intensity affects cryptochrome-dependent responses in Arabidopsis thaliana. [10.1007/s00425-006-0383-0] Solovyov2007: Theoretical analysis of Arabidopsis cryptochrome-1 shows magnetic fields could alter activation yields through radical-pair spin dynamics. [10.1529/biophysj.106.097139] Harris2009: Under blinded conditions, cryptochrome-dependent magnetic-field effects in Arabidopsis were NOT reproduced. [10.1098/rsif.2008.0519] Pooam2019: Magnetic sensitivity mediated by Arabidopsis cryptochrome occurs during flavin reoxidation in the dark, not during photoreduction. [10.1007/s00425-018-3002-y] Xu2014: Blue-light-dependent phosphorylation of cryptochromes is affected by magnetic fields in Arabidopsis. [10.1016/j.asr.2014.01.033] rationale: The reference case for the radical-pair mechanism in biology, and the entity from which the review's whole argument is generalised outward.
caveat: Direction of effect is not consistent across the literature, and one blinded replication attempt failed (see Harris2009 below). Treat the magnitude as unsettled even though the mechanism is well characterised.

Complex I (NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: flavin_semiquinone, iron_sulfur_4Fe4S, iron_sulfur_2Fe2S, ros_leak_site nuclei: 1H, 14N, 57Fe, 33S AGI: AT5G37510, AT5G08530, AT4G02580, AT5G11770 rationale: The FMN site forms a flavin semiquinone during turnover and is a known superoxide-producing leak site, and the Fe/S chain performs sequential one-electron transfers — both of the physical routes the radical-pair and hyperfine arguments require. No published experiment has applied a near-null field and measured plant complex I activity, so this is a hypothesis with a mechanism, not a result.
caveat: Electron transfer along the Fe/S chain is fast relative to plausible singlet-triplet mixing times, so a coherent radical-pair effect here is harder to argue than at the flavin. Treat the flavin and the cluster chain as separate hypotheses rather than one.

Rieske [2Fe-2S] centre (complex III) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: rieske_2Fe2S, semiquinone_radical, ros_leak_site nuclei: 57Fe, 33S, 1H AGI: AT5G13430, AT5G13440 rationale: The Qo site generates a kinetically stabilised ubisemiquinone — a genuine, comparatively long-lived organic radical in a defined protein pocket, which is the most favourable setting for a field-dependent branching effect anywhere in the respiratory chain.
caveat: Qo-site semiquinone is short-lived and its occupancy is debated; a field effect here would be easier to argue if lifetime were measured under the relevant conditions.

Photosystem I Fe/S centres (FX, FA, FB) tier T2 (reported) quantum class: iron_sulfur_4Fe4S, radical_pair_acceptor, triplet_yield_sensitive nuclei: 57Fe, 33S, 1H AGI: ATCG01060 Parmagnani2023: The geomagnetic field is required for normal lima bean photosynthesis, PSI/LHCI content and ROS production; near-null field conditions altered photosynthetic electron transport. [10.3390/ijms24032896] rationale: PSI is the strongest structural case in the whole atlas. Charge separation at P700 produces a genuine spin-correlated radical pair (P700·+ A1·−), which is the textbook example of the species the radical-pair mechanism describes — it is studied by exactly that formalism in photosynthesis spectroscopy. Three [4Fe-4S] clusters then carry the electron onward.
caveat: The P700·+ A1·− pair is extremely short-lived, and the well-characterised magnetic-field effects on it are seen in isolated preparations at fields far above geomagnetic. Structural plausibility is high; relevance at 50 uT is not established.

Cellular Fe / S supply tier T2 (verified) quantum class: structural_context Islam2020: The geomagnetic field contributes to efficient iron uptake in Arabidopsis; reducing it to near-null affects root metal reductase activity. [10.3389/fpls.2020.00325] Vigani2021: Geomagnetic-field-dependent modulation of iron-sulfur interplay in Arabidopsis, most pronounced under combined Fe and S deficiency. [10.3390/ijms221810166] Narayana2018: Reduction of the geomagnetic field to near-null affects Arabidopsis root mineral nutrition. [10.1016/j.lssr.2018.08.005] rationale: Note carefully what the cited work does and does not show. Islam 2020 and Vigani 2021 measured iron uptake and Fe-S interplay under altered field conditions — nutritional physiology. Neither measured cluster assembly. This entity is T2 because the field effect is demonstrated for the process it names; the assembly entities above remain T3 because that evidence does not reach them.

Singlet ⇄ triplet interconversion tier T2 (reported) quantum class: triplet_yield_sensitive, spin_correlated_pair, hyperfine_coupled nuclei: 1H, 14N Ritz2000: A photoreceptor-based radical-pair model can in principle transduce a geomagnetic-strength field into a change in signalling yield. [10.1016/S0006-3495(00)76629-X] ZadehHaghighi2022: Review of magnetic field effects in biology from the radical-pair perspective, covering the lifetime and hyperfine conditions required. [10.1098/rsif.2022.0325] rationale: This is the mechanism itself rather than a molecule. It is on the map because the review's argument is that this step, not the protein, is what generalises to other flavoproteins and Fe/S centres.
caveat: For a field of geomagnetic magnitude to compete, the radical pair must live long enough for mixing to accumulate — roughly the microsecond scale. That lifetime requirement is what most candidate sites elsewhere in this atlas have not been shown to meet.

Fe/S client proteins tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: iron_sulfur_4Fe4S, iron_sulfur_2Fe2S nuclei: 57Fe, 33S AGI: AT4G35830, AT5G66760, AT5G13430, AT4G03280, AT1G10960, AT2G20860, AT2G21790 rationale: Collected here so the map can show, in one edge, that a single assembly defect reaches respiration, photosynthesis, the TCA cycle, nitrogen and sulfur assimilation and DNA replication simultaneously. That breadth is the review's argument for why Fe/S biology deserves attention ahead of cryptochrome.

Mitochondrial superoxide / H2O2 tier T2 (reported) quantum class: ros_leak_site AGI: AT3G10920 Parmagnani2022: Near-null magnetic field exposure alters ROS-associated transcriptomic and metabolomic programmes in Arabidopsis. [10.3390/biom12121824] Farooq2021: Reactive oxygen species and mitochondria jointly regulate seed germination, establishing the route from mitochondrial ROS to a developmental outcome. [10.3389/fpls.2021.781734] rationale: Not a magnetosensitive mechanism itself — it is the amplifier. A field effect too small to measure as a rate change can still register here, because ROS signalling is threshold-like.
Primary metabolism tier T4 (inferred) quantum class: structural_context

ROS-responsive transcriptional programme tier T2 (verified) quantum class: structural_context Parmagnani2022: Transcriptomics and metabolomics of ROS modulation in near-null magnetic field-induced Arabidopsis: field reduction alters ROS-associated transcriptional and metabolic programmes. [10.3390/biom12121824] Zsigmond2008: Arabidopsis PPR40 connects abiotic stress responses to mitochondrial electron transport, establishing a route from respiratory state to stress signalling. [10.1104/pp.107.111260] rationale: This entity carries demonstrated near-null-field evidence but NO proposed quantum route, and is classed structural_context to say so explicitly. It is the amplifier's output: threshold-like signalling turns an upstream change too small to measure directly into a transcriptional response. That sensitivity is what makes it the best-evidenced node in the atlas and simultaneously a poor discriminator — it reports that something moved upstream, never what.

Gibberellin signalling (GA3OX1, GA20OX1, RGA, GAI, RGL2) tier T2 (verified) quantum class: structural_context AGI: AT1G15550, AT4G25420, AT2G01570, AT1G14920, AT3G03450 Xu2017: Gibberellins are involved in the effect of a near-null magnetic field on Arabidopsis flowering. [10.1002/bem.22004] rationale: Demonstrated field evidence with no proposed quantum route. Xu et al. showed gibberellins are involved in the near-null-field effect on flowering, which makes this a real link in the causal chain — but GA signalling is ubiquitin-proteasome chemistry with no radical or metal centre, so no mechanism is claimed.

Auxin transport and signalling (PIN1/2/3, AUX1, TIR1, ARF7) tier T2 (verified) quantum class: structural_context AGI: AT1G73590, AT5G57090, AT1G70940, AT2G38120, AT3G62980, AT5G20730 Xu2018: Suppression of Arabidopsis flowering by a near-null magnetic field is mediated by auxin. [10.1002/bem.22086] Xu2021: A near-null magnetic field suppresses fruit growth in Arabidopsis. [10.1002/bem.22363] rationale: As with gibberellin: a demonstrated field effect with no proposed spin route. Xu et al. showed auxin mediates near-null-field suppression of flowering.

Circadian clock (CCA1, LHY, TOC1, PRR5/7/9, GI, ELF4) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: structural_context AGI: AT2G46830, AT1G01060, AT5G61380, AT5G24470, AT5G02810, AT2G46790, AT1G22770, AT2G40080 rationale: No spin route of its own, and no direct field measurement on clock components in the bibliography. It is on the map because cryptochrome is a clock input, so a field effect at CRY would necessarily arrive here — and because a clock is a gate, meaning the same perturbation can produce opposite outcomes depending on when it is applied. That alone could explain some of the inconsistency in near-null-field results, and it is testable.
caveat: This is the atlas's most speculative causal claim and is flagged as such. It is offered as an experimental design consideration, not a finding.

Radicle emergence tier T4 (reported) quantum class: structural_context Farooq2021: Reactive oxygen species and mitochondria jointly regulate seed germination, defining the window in which a respiratory lesion would have most leverage. [10.3389/fpls.2021.781734] Eckardt2005: Peroxisomal citrate synthase provides the exit route from fatty acid metabolism in oilseeds, linking reserve mobilisation to the TCA cycle. [10.1105/tpc.105.034843]

Flowering time (CO → FT) tier T4 (reported) quantum class: structural_context Agliassa2018a: Reduction of the geomagnetic field to below 100 nT delayed Arabidopsis flowering and downregulated flowering-related genes. [10.1002/bem.22123] Xu2015: Suppression of Arabidopsis flowering by a near-null magnetic field depends on the light conditions. [10.1002/bem.21927] Xu2013: Removal of the local geomagnetic field affected reproductive growth, including silique number and seed yield. [10.1002/bem.21788]

Reproductive output (siliques, seed yield) tier T2 (verified) quantum class: structural_context Xu2013: Removal of the local geomagnetic field affects reproductive growth in Arabidopsis, reducing silique number and seed yield. [10.1002/bem.21788] Xu2021: Near-null magnetic field suppresses fruit growth in Arabidopsis. [10.1002/bem.22363] rationale: A phenotype with demonstrated field evidence and, necessarily, no quantum route of its own. It is the accumulated consequence of everything upstream, which is what makes it reproducible and also what makes it uninformative about mechanism.
Brassica crop translation tier T4 (inferred) quantum class: structural_context

svg.text: The flagship map, and the one that has to be read most carefully. The review states that its Figure 7 is designed for hypothesis generation and
experimental planning rather than as a proven causal network, and the tiers here preserve that distinction: the input perturbation and the developmental
outputs carry real evidence, while the molecular route between them does not. Read the border styles from left to right and the shape of the field's
problem is visible — the evidence is concentrated at the two ends, on the perturbation and on the phenotypes, while the middle, where the mechanism
would have to live, is almost entirely dashed. Primary metabolism, the review's central thesis, is drawn as T4 on purpose: the metabolic route is argued
rather than demonstrated, and the map should not let it borrow credibility from the developmental evidence beside it. The model is explicitly modular —
cryptochrome may dominate in blue-light-grown seedlings, mitochondria in dark-imbibed seeds, plastids in greening tissue, and nutrient uptake in roots —
so a single phenotype may be produced by different weightings of the same components depending on tissue, stage and light regime. Derived from:
Figure 7 of Porterfield & Barker, "Plant Responses to Near-Null Magnetic Fields" — expanded and tier-annotated. Node counts by evidence tier: T1=1,
T2=8, T3=4, T4=6. Schematic topology only — no quantitative value is encoded in this base map; numbers appear only when measured data is projected
onto it. Values are the authors' published results from Agliassa, Narayana, Bertea, Rodgers & Maffei (2018), Bioelectromagnetics 39(5):361-374
(doi:10.1002/bem.22123), not a reanalysis: NNMF-grown plants relative to GMF controls at the equivalent timepoint. No raw data was deposited — the
Data Availability Statement reads “no Data Availability Statement is present in the article; the quantitative data appear only as main-text tables”.
Reported as log2 fold change; values are signed fold change — never reported strictly between -1 and +1 — so a negative number is a reciprocal, not a
log. leaves, 6 timepoints (17, 19, 21, 22, 23, 28). 2 of 9 identifier-bearing nodes received a series (22%); 10 nodes carry no gene identifier and cannot.
multi-locus nodes aggregated by extreme at each timepoint. 1 node(s) have loci that disagree in direction at the same timepoint (CIRCADIAN_CLOCK), so
their single trace is the aggregator choosing between genes that are doing different things — read those per locus, not as a node. 1 node(s) reverse
direction during the course (GA_SIGNALLING), which no single-contrast overlay can show. Each node is tinted by its most extreme timepoint. A node
standing for ONE locus carries a sparkline of its trajectory — the colour says how far it moved, the line says when. A node standing for SEVERAL carries a
per-locus heatmap instead, one row per locus and one column per timepoint, because an aggregate cannot show a gene family splitting and under a
strong perturbation families do split. A node with no measurement is left unfilled, which is not the same as a measured zero.

g.text: one row per locus, one column per timepoint, earliest left — so a gene family that splits shows as a warm row above a cool one, which the
